paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: looking at somebody else's easy life can knock you off your feet, but the answer isn't a better view of THEM. It's a better view of God. Asaph says his feet had almost stumbled when he envied the arrogant (Psalm 73:2-3). Envy tells you the people ignoring God are winning, and it will keep telling you that all day long.

Asaph couldn't think his way out of it. He says it was troublesome in his sight "until I entered God's sanctuary; then I discerned their end" (Psalm 73:16-17). The picture changed when he came into God's presence, not when he got more information. So when your head is spinning, I'd say go where God is: His Word, His people, prayer. Then look at things again.

And look where Asaph lands. He admits he was senseless, a brute beast before God, and then he says, "Yet I am always with You; You hold my right hand" (Psalm 73:22-23). God held on to him while he was a mess, and that's the good news for every baker with a wobbly heart. His ending is that "it is good to draw near to God" (Psalm 73:28), and I'm telling you, that's a better portion than anything the carefree crowd has got.
